The quotation “Let them eat cake” (originally “Qu’ils mangent de la brioche”) first appears in Jean‑Jacques Rousseau’s *Confessions* (written ca. 1765). Rousseau records that a “princess of the blood” responded to news of a bread shortage with that remark. Because the passage predates Marie Antoinette’s arrival in France, she could not have been the speaker, and no contemporary source links the phrase to her. Scholars therefore conclude that Rousseau attributed the statement to an unnamed princess—often conjectured to be Maria Theresa of Spain (the wife of Louis XIV) or another earlier royal figure.
